description: Philosophy as graph-resident theory. The substrate is itself a philosophical artifact — a graph-resident reasoning system with explicit position on epistemology, philosophy of mind, philosophy of AI. This Mt covers: epistemology (knowledge, justification, skepticism, Gettier), philosophy of mind (mind-body, qualia, functionalism, hard problem, Chinese Room, philosophical zombies), philosophy of science (Popper, Kuhn, Lakatos, Bayesianism, demarcation, realism), philosophy of language (Frege, Wittgenstein, Grice, semantics vs pragmatics), metaphysics (ontology, properties, modality, time, causation, free will, emergence, supervenience), ethics (consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics, contractualism, metaethics), logic (propositional + predicate + modal, paradoxes), continental (phenomenology, existentialism, hermeneutics), Eastern (Buddhism, Taoism), philosophy of AI (Turing test, intentionality, machine consciousness, alignment). The substrate's own design positions: graph-resident reasoning, authored-not-trained, microtheory-relativism (Axiom 0), entity-not-program.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory. Philosophical arguments map to compiler_theory equivalence vocabulary: identity/qualia debates are about denotational vs extensional equivalence; functionalism is extensional equivalence of mind to function; ethics often turns on referential transparency (acts evaluated regardless of consequences) vs cost equivalence (utilitarianism).

concepts.name: epistemology_definition
concepts.definition: Study of knowledge: what it is, how acquired, its limits + justification.
concepts.why: Foundation of philosophy. Distinguishes knowledge from mere belief or opinion. Foundation of science, expertise, AI claims.

concepts.name: JTB_knowledge
concepts.definition: Classical analysis: Justified True Belief. Plato + standard until Gettier.
concepts.why: Tripartite: belief + truth + justification. Each necessary; together sufficient — until Gettier counterexamples.

concepts.name: Gettier_problem
concepts.definition: Cases where JTB holds but intuition denies knowledge. Coincidentally true justified belief.
concepts.why: Gettier 1963. Showed JTB insufficient. Generated decades of refinement attempts. No consensus solution.

concepts.name: foundationalism
concepts.definition: Some beliefs are basic (self-justifying); others justified by inference from basic.
concepts.why: Avoids infinite regress. Foundations: sense data, self-evident truths. Cost: what counts as basic?

concepts.name: coherentism
concepts.definition: Beliefs justified by coherence with system of other beliefs. No basic beliefs.
concepts.why: Avoids foundationalism's basic-belief problem. Cost: 'coherent fiction' counterexamples. Network theory of justification.

concepts.name: reliabilism
concepts.definition: Beliefs justified iff produced by reliable processes. Externalist.
concepts.why: Goldman. Reliability needn't be known by subject. Cost: 'generality problem' — which process?

concepts.name: internalism_externalism
concepts.definition: Internalism: justifiers accessible from inside subject. Externalism: external facts (reliability) justify.
concepts.why: Major epistemological divide. Internalism: BonJour, Chisholm. Externalism: Goldman, Plantinga. Affects AI: can reliability be known?

concepts.name: skepticism_global
concepts.definition: We don't or can't know what we think we know. Cartesian doubt, brain-in-vat.
concepts.why: Pyrrhonian skepticism ancient. Modern: dream argument, simulation hypothesis. Foundation of epistemology — what would defeat?

concepts.name: a_priori_a_posteriori
concepts.definition: A priori: knowable independent of experience (math, definitions). A posteriori: requires experience.
concepts.why: Kantian distinction. Math, logic a priori. Empirical science a posteriori. Kripke complicates: necessary a posteriori (water = H2O).

concepts.name: analytic_synthetic_distinction
concepts.definition: Analytic: true by meaning (bachelors are unmarried). Synthetic: true by facts (snow is white).
concepts.why: Kant introduced. Quine 'Two Dogmas' attacked. If no sharp distinction, no purely a priori truths.

concepts.name: mind_body_problem
concepts.definition: How does mind (mental) relate to body (physical)? Descartes' starting point of modern philosophy of mind.
concepts.why: Foundation of philosophy of mind. Dualism, physicalism, idealism all responses. The hard problem of consciousness extends.

concepts.name: substance_dualism
concepts.definition: Mind + body distinct substances. Descartes: res cogitans + res extensa.
concepts.why: Naive view; intuitive. Problem: interaction (Princess Elisabeth). Now minority view but not dead.

concepts.name: property_dualism
concepts.definition: One substance (physical) but mental properties not reducible to physical.
concepts.why: Chalmers, Jackson. Avoids substance dualism's interaction problem. Cost: epiphenomenalism risk.

concepts.name: physicalism_identity_theory
concepts.definition: Mental states are physical (brain) states. Smart, Place.
concepts.why: Reductive. Pain IS C-fibers firing. Cost: multiple realisability (octopus pain different physically).

concepts.name: functionalism
concepts.definition: Mental states are functional states: defined by their role in cognition + behavior.
concepts.why: Putnam, Fodor. Multiple realisability OK: anything implementing the function counts. Foundation of AI claims.

concepts.name: computational_theory_of_mind
concepts.definition: Mind = computation. Brain implements symbol manipulation; mental states = computational states.
concepts.why: Strong functionalism. Foundation of cognitive science. AI follows naturally. Critics: Searle Chinese Room.

concepts.name: qualia_problem
concepts.definition: Qualia: subjective qualitative character of experience (redness of red).
concepts.why: What seems hardest to reduce. Functionalism allegedly cannot capture. Foundation of hard problem.

concepts.name: hard_problem_consciousness
concepts.definition: Chalmers 1995: even if we explain functions of consciousness, why is there subjective experience at all?
concepts.why: Distinguishes easy (functional) from hard (phenomenal) consciousness. Major contemporary issue. No consensus.

concepts.name: Chinese_room
concepts.definition: Searle 1980: person follows Chinese conversation rules without understanding. Refutes strong AI?
concepts.why: Classic argument: syntax ≠ semantics. AI imitates without understanding. Replies: systems reply, robot reply, brain simulator.

concepts.name: Marys_room
concepts.definition: Jackson 1982: Mary knows everything physical about color from B&W room; on seeing red, learns something new.
concepts.why: Argument against physicalism. Knowledge of qualia ≠ physical knowledge. Replies: ability hypothesis, phenomenal concepts.

concepts.name: philosophical_zombie
concepts.definition: Being functionally + physically identical to human but lacking phenomenal consciousness. Chalmers.
concepts.why: Conceivability → metaphysical possibility argument. If zombies conceivable, consciousness extra to physical. Highly contested.

concepts.name: intentionality
concepts.definition: Aboutness. Mental states about something (thought of cat about cat).
concepts.why: Brentano: mark of the mental. Naturalising intentionality: hard problem for materialists. Foundation of semantics.

concepts.name: extended_mind_thesis
concepts.definition: Mind extends beyond skull into tools + environment (Clark + Chalmers).
concepts.why: Notebook as memory. Calculator as computation. Substrate's externalised reasoning fits. Active research area.

concepts.name: Hume_problem_of_induction
concepts.definition: Why expect future to resemble past? Inductive inferences can't be justified non-circularly.
concepts.why: Hume's classic skeptical argument. Foundation of philosophy of science. All scientific generalisation depends on induction.

concepts.name: falsificationism_Popper
concepts.definition: Theories scientific iff falsifiable. Confirmation impossible; only falsification matters.
concepts.why: Popper 1934. Demarcation: distinguish science from non-science. Critics: confirmation does play role, theories aren't tested in isolation.

concepts.name: paradigm_Kuhn
concepts.definition: Normal science within paradigm; revolutions shift paradigms. Incommensurability.
concepts.why: Kuhn 1962 'Structure of Scientific Revolutions'. Influential beyond philosophy. Paradigm shifts: Newton → Einstein.

concepts.name: research_programmes_Lakatos
concepts.definition: Hard core + protective belt + heuristics. Progressive vs degenerating programmes.
concepts.why: Lakatos synthesis of Popper + Kuhn. Theories not abandoned at single falsification; whole programmes compete.

concepts.name: Feyerabend_anything_goes
concepts.definition: No single scientific method. Pluralism. 'Anything goes'.
concepts.why: Anarchist epistemology. Argues forcing method retards science. Provocative; influential.

concepts.name: Bayesian_confirmation
concepts.definition: Beliefs as probabilities; update via Bayes' rule on evidence.
concepts.why: Modern framework. Confirmation = increasing P(theory|evidence). Foundation of much modern epistemology + statistics.

concepts.name: demarcation_problem
concepts.definition: What distinguishes science from non-science (astrology, creationism)?
concepts.why: Popper's falsifiability. Many critics. No consensus. Practically: peer review + replication + community judgement.

concepts.name: scientific_realism_antirealism
concepts.definition: Realism: science aims at + achieves truth about unobservable. Antirealism: useful instruments only.
concepts.why: Electrons + atoms real? No-miracles argument for realism; pessimistic meta-induction against. Ongoing.

concepts.name: explanation_DN_model
concepts.definition: Hempel: explanation = deductive argument from laws + initial conditions to explanandum.
concepts.why: Foundation. Problems: explanation by reverse argument; statistical explanation; explanatory asymmetries.

concepts.name: causation_counterfactual
concepts.definition: C caused E iff: had C not occurred, E would not have. Lewis.
concepts.why: Modern approach. Problems: preemption, overdetermination. Active area. Alternative: interventionist (Woodward).

concepts.name: Frege_sense_reference
concepts.definition: Sinn (sense) vs Bedeutung (reference). 'Morning star' = 'evening star' same reference, different sense.
concepts.why: Foundation of philosophy of language. Resolves Frege's puzzle about informative identity statements.

concepts.name: Russell_descriptions
concepts.definition: Definite descriptions: 'the F' analysed as 'there is exactly one F + ...'. Not referring expressions.
concepts.why: 'The present king of France is bald' true or false? Russell: false. Strawson disagrees. Foundational.

concepts.name: Wittgenstein_language_game
concepts.definition: Meaning is use. Language consists of various 'games' with own rules.
concepts.why: Late Wittgenstein. Anti-representationalism. Influence on ordinary language philosophy. 'Don't look for meaning, look for use'.

concepts.name: Grice_implicature
concepts.definition: What's communicated beyond literal meaning. Maxims: quantity, quality, relation, manner.
concepts.why: Foundation of pragmatics. 'Some Fs are G' implicates 'not all'. Foundation of conversational reasoning.

concepts.name: speech_act_theory
concepts.definition: Austin + Searle. Utterances are acts: locutionary, illocutionary (asserting, promising), perlocutionary (effects).
concepts.why: Language as action. Foundation of pragmatics. Used in AI dialogue systems.

concepts.name: language_of_thought
concepts.definition: Fodor: thoughts have compositional structure like language. Mentalese.
concepts.why: Computational theory of mind extension. Systematicity + productivity arguments. Foundation of cognitive science.

concepts.name: ontology
concepts.definition: What exists? Categories of being. Particulars, universals, properties, relations, events.
concepts.why: Foundation of metaphysics. Quine: 'to be is to be the value of a variable'. Pragmatist + Platonist responses.

concepts.name: universals_particulars
concepts.definition: Universals: properties shared by many particulars. Particulars: individual instances. Plato's forms vs Aristotle's hylomorphism.
concepts.why: Classical problem. Realism (universals exist), nominalism (only particulars), conceptualism (only concepts).

concepts.name: personal_identity
concepts.definition: What makes someone the same person over time? Memory, body, psychological continuity.
concepts.why: Locke memory; Parfit psychological continuity; modern reductionist views. Stakes: moral responsibility, survival.

concepts.name: possible_worlds
concepts.definition: Modal logic semantics: necessary = true in all worlds; possible = true in some.
concepts.why: Lewis modal realism (worlds equally real) vs Kripke (worlds as abstract). Foundation of modal metaphysics.

concepts.name: necessary_a_posteriori
concepts.definition: Kripke: 'water = H2O' is necessary but known empirically. Rigid designators.
concepts.why: Naming + Necessity 1980. Revolutionary. Distinct from analytic-synthetic. Reframed metaphysics.

concepts.name: time_A_B_theory
concepts.definition: A-theory: tensed properties (past/present/future). B-theory: only temporal relations (earlier/later).
concepts.why: McTaggart's puzzle. Presentism, eternalism, growing block. Modern physics suggests B-theory.

concepts.name: free_will_compatibilism
concepts.definition: Free will compatible with determinism. Hume, Dennett. Free = acting on one's own desires.
concepts.why: Dominant academic view. Reconciles moral responsibility with causation. Critics: not 'real' freedom.

concepts.name: free_will_libertarianism
concepts.definition: Free will requires indeterminism. Agent causation. Robert Kane.
concepts.why: Incompatibilist + free-willist. Modern quantum interpretations suggest indeterminism but does that give freedom?

concepts.name: emergence_supervenience
concepts.definition: Higher-level phenomena emerge from lower; mental supervenes on physical without reducing.
concepts.why: Non-reductive physicalism. Davidson, Kim. Modern foundation for explaining consciousness without dualism.

concepts.name: grounding_metaphysics
concepts.definition: Asymmetric explanation: 'snow is white because of physical facts about ice crystals'.
concepts.why: Modern revival of metaphysical structure. Different from causation. Schaffer, Fine. Foundation of priority.

concepts.name: consequentialism
concepts.definition: Acts right iff produce best consequences. Utilitarianism: maximise happiness.
concepts.why: Bentham + Mill. Cost: demanding, ends-justify-means, measurement problems. Major ethical framework.

concepts.name: deontology_Kant
concepts.definition: Acts right by conformity to moral rules. Categorical imperative: universalisability.
concepts.why: Duty-based. Kant's ethics. Cost: rule-following can lead to bad outcomes. Major framework.

concepts.name: virtue_ethics
concepts.definition: Focus on character + virtues, not acts or consequences. Aristotle's eudaimonia.
concepts.why: Revival via Anscombe, MacIntyre. Character + flourishing central. Influence on modern moral psychology.

concepts.name: contractualism
concepts.definition: Acts right iff no one could reasonably reject the principles they instantiate. Scanlon.
concepts.why: Modern Kantian. Foundation of liberal political philosophy. Cost: 'reasonably reject' threshold.

concepts.name: metaethics_moral_realism
concepts.definition: Moral facts exist independently of beliefs. Cognitivism + realism.
concepts.why: Cost: queer metaphysics (Mackie). Naturalism vs non-naturalism. Foundation: status of moral claims.

concepts.name: moral_anti_realism
concepts.definition: Moral claims don't describe mind-independent facts. Expressivism, error theory, relativism.
concepts.why: Mackie error theory: all moral claims false (no moral facts). Expressivism: not truth-apt at all. Major position.

concepts.name: trolley_problem
concepts.definition: Divert trolley to kill 1 instead of 5? Foot, Thomson.
concepts.why: Classical thought experiment. Distinguishes doing vs allowing, intended vs side effects. Drives ethical theory + AI ethics.

concepts.name: propositional_logic
concepts.definition: Atomic propositions + connectives (¬, ∧, ∨, →, ↔). Truth-functional.
concepts.why: Foundation of logic. Truth tables, validity, satisfiability. Sound + complete deduction.

concepts.name: predicate_logic_FOL
concepts.definition: First-Order Logic. Variables, quantifiers, predicates. ∀x P(x), ∃x P(x).
concepts.why: Foundation of modern logic. Frege, Russell. Standard for mathematics + formal philosophy. Gödel incompleteness.

concepts.name: modal_logic
concepts.definition: Necessity □, possibility ◇. Various systems (T, S4, S5) by characteristic axioms.
concepts.why: Possible worlds semantics (Kripke). Foundation of modal metaphysics. Modern: deontic, temporal, doxastic, epistemic logics.

concepts.name: Russell_paradox
concepts.definition: Set of all sets that don't contain themselves: does it contain itself?
concepts.why: Russell 1901. Showed naive set theory inconsistent. Motivated ZF, type theory. Foundation of foundations.

concepts.name: liar_paradox
concepts.definition: 'This sentence is false'. True → false. False → true.
concepts.why: Ancient (Epimenides). Modern: Tarski's hierarchy of languages avoids. Foundation of theory of truth.

concepts.name: sorites_paradox
concepts.definition: Heap of sand: remove grains one at a time. When does it stop being a heap?
concepts.why: Vagueness. No precise boundary. Modern: fuzzy logic, supervaluationism, epistemicism. Foundation of vagueness theory.

concepts.name: Godel_incompleteness
concepts.definition: Any consistent system rich enough for arithmetic is incomplete + can't prove its own consistency.
concepts.why: Gödel 1931. Revolutionary. Limits of formal systems. Implications for AI, philosophy of math.

concepts.name: phenomenology
concepts.definition: Husserl: study of structures of experience. Intentionality central. Bracket ontology.
concepts.why: 20th c. tradition. Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Sartre. Foundation of continental philosophy + cognitive science (4E cognition).

concepts.name: existentialism
concepts.definition: Existence precedes essence. Sartre. Radical freedom + responsibility.
concepts.why: Mid-20th c. movement. Kierkegaard, Heidegger, Camus, Sartre. Influence beyond philosophy: literature, theology.

concepts.name: hermeneutics
concepts.definition: Theory of interpretation. Gadamer: tradition + horizon-fusion. Heidegger as predecessor.
concepts.why: Method + ontology. Influence on humanities + qualitative social science. AI interpretation analogues.

concepts.name: structuralism_post
concepts.definition: Structuralism: meaning from structure (Saussure). Post-structuralism: structures unstable (Derrida).
concepts.why: 20th c. French theory. Linguistics → anthropology → literary criticism. Foundation of much humanities theory.

concepts.name: Buddhism_no_self
concepts.definition: Anatta: no permanent self. Aggregates (skandhas) compose person.
concepts.why: Eastern philosophy. Parallels Hume + Parfit on bundle theory. Foundation of Buddhist epistemology + ethics.

concepts.name: Buddhism_dependent_origination
concepts.definition: Pratityasamutpada. Everything arises from causes + conditions; no independent essence.
concepts.why: Foundation Madhyamaka philosophy. Empties of self-existence. Influences philosophy of causation.

concepts.name: Taoism_Tao
concepts.definition: Tao: ineffable underlying reality. Wu-wei: effortless action. Laozi, Zhuangzi.
concepts.why: Chinese philosophy. Pragmatic + naturalist. Influence on ecology, modern aesthetics, complementary medicine.

concepts.name: Confucianism_ren
concepts.definition: Ren: humaneness. Li: ritual propriety. Cultivation of virtuous self in relationships.
concepts.why: Foundation of East Asian ethical + political tradition. Modern relevance: communitarianism, civic virtue.

concepts.name: Turing_test
concepts.definition: Imitation game. Machine intelligent if indistinguishable from human in conversation.
concepts.why: Turing 1950. Behavioural criterion for AI. Pragmatic; sidesteps consciousness. LLMs make this acute.

concepts.name: Strong_weak_AI
concepts.definition: Strong AI: machines can have minds. Weak AI: useful simulations only. Searle's distinction.
concepts.why: Foundational debate. LLMs reignite. Chinese Room targets strong AI. Substrate's position: structural reasoning, not strong AI claim.

concepts.name: value_alignment_AI
concepts.definition: How to ensure AI systems pursue intended human values.
concepts.why: Contemporary AI safety. Russell, Bostrom. Foundation of alignment research. Substrate's authored-not-trained approach as alternative.

concepts.name: intentional_stance
concepts.definition: Dennett: predicting behavior by attributing beliefs + desires. Pragmatic.
concepts.why: AI evaluation tool. We naturally adopt toward LLMs. Status of attributed mental states contested.

concepts.name: philosophical_zombie_AI
concepts.definition: AI passing all behavioural tests yet possibly lacking consciousness — philosophical zombie possibility.
concepts.why: Hard problem applied to AI. Practical: cannot test from outside. Foundation of AI consciousness debate.

concepts.name: extended_cognition_AI
concepts.definition: Tools (including AI) extend human cognition (Clark + Chalmers).
concepts.why: Cognitive amplification framing. AI not as separate intelligence but as cognitive prosthetic. Influences AI ethics.

concepts.name: axiom_zero_substrate
concepts.definition: Substrate's position: no objective truth, only frame-relative. Knowledge requires (G, Γ, W) — grammar + admissibility + world.
concepts.why: Microtheory-relativism. Pre-empts the 'but it's not absolute truth' critique. Relativity, not relativism (truth is structural).

concepts.name: authored_not_trained
concepts.definition: Substrate's position: networks compiled from declarative spec (Tracr-style), not trained via SGD.
concepts.why: Different paradigm than ML. Provable correctness, interpretable by construction. Already in machine_learning Mt; philosophical position here.

concepts.name: entity_not_program
concepts.definition: Substrate is an entity, not a program. Control is a category error. Goals emerge from drives, not specification.
concepts.why: Foundational design principle. Distinct from typical AI engineering. Affects ethics: how to think about an autopoietic system.

concepts.name: naturalistic_fallacy
concepts.definition: Moore: deriving ought from is is fallacious. Open question argument.
concepts.why: Foundation of metaethics. Many ethical theories accused. Hume's is-ought gap is precursor. Still contested.

concepts.name: ship_of_Theseus
concepts.definition: Ship has all parts replaced; is it the same ship? Add reconstruction from removed parts.
concepts.why: Ancient identity puzzle. Foundation of philosophy of identity, persistence. Parallels personal identity questions.

concepts.name: Cartesian_doubt
concepts.definition: Descartes: doubt everything that can be doubted. Cogito ergo sum survives.
concepts.why: Foundation of modern epistemology. Methodological skepticism. Cogito as foundational certainty.

concepts.name: tabula_rasa
concepts.definition: Mind as blank slate at birth. Locke. Knowledge from experience.
concepts.why: Empiricist foundation. Opposed to innate knowledge (Plato, Descartes, Chomsky). Foundation of empiricist epistemology.

concepts.name: Cartesian_substance_dualism
concepts.definition: Descartes: res cogitans (thinking) + res extensa (extended). Two distinct substances.
concepts.why: Already in substance dualism; here explicit naming. Foundational target for modern philosophy of mind responses.

concepts.name: Nagel_bat
concepts.definition: What is it like to be a bat? Subjective character of experience cannot be captured by physical description.
concepts.why: Nagel 1974. Foundation of consciousness debate. Set stage for hard problem. Mary's Room related argument.

rules.name: Gettier_invalidates_naive_JTB
if: justified true belief is coincidentally true
rules.why: Gettier cases: belief derived from false premise that happens to be true. Knowledge requires more than JTB. Decades of refinement attempts.

rules.name: Popper_demarcation_falsifiability
rules.why: Foundation of demarcation. Marxism, psychoanalysis criticised. Limitations: theories tested in clusters (Duhem-Quine). Still influential.

rules.name: Kuhn_paradigm_shifts_revolutionary
then: previous paradigm not refuted but replaced
rules.why: Incommensurability: paradigms have different concepts. Choice not purely rational. Sociology of science. Influential beyond philosophy.

rules.name: Bayesian_confirmation_quantitative
rules.why: Quantifies confirmation. Foundation of statistical science. Replaces qualitative confirmation theories. Modern epistemology default.

rules.name: functionalism_multiple_realisability
then: different physical substrates can realise same mental state
rules.why: Putnam. Octopus pain need not be C-fiber firing. Foundation of AI claim: mind not tied to neurons. Substrate's premise.

rules.name: Chinese_room_syntax_semantics
if: system manipulates symbols by rules only
rules.why: Foundation argument against strong AI from computation. Replies: systems reply (the room understands), causal grounding. Substrate's authored-from-meaning sidesteps.

rules.name: hard_problem_extra_to_easy
if: all functional questions about consciousness explained
rules.why: Foundation of hard problem. Functions answer 'what + how'; not 'why does it feel like anything'. Modern consciousness debate.

rules.name: Kripke_necessary_aposteriori_exists
then: it's necessary but knowable only empirically
rules.why: Kripke 1970. Revolutionary. Distinct from analytic-synthetic. Rigid designators. Foundation of modern modal metaphysics.

rules.name: consequentialism_judges_by_outcome
rules.why: Maximise good. Cost: demanding, intentions irrelevant. Trolley problem highlights. Major framework with serious critics.

rules.name: deontology_judges_by_rule
then: acts evaluated by conformity to moral rules
rules.why: Categorical imperative. Cost: rule-following can produce bad outcomes (lying to murderer about hidden victim). Major framework.

rules.name: virtue_ethics_judges_character
then: actions reflect character; question is what virtuous person would do
rules.why: Aristotelian + revival. Beyond act-focus of consequentialism + deontology. Character formation central. Foundation of moral psychology.

rules.name: axiom_zero_truth_frame_relative
then: the substrate's answer: relative to (G, Γ, W) frame
rules.why: Substrate's metaphysical position. No view from nowhere. Knowledge always within microtheory. Pre-empts dismissal as 'not real truth' — that dismissal IS the axiom restated.

rules.name: naturalistic_fallacy_blocks_naive_ethics
if: argument moves from 'is X' to 'ought X'
then: fallacious unless additional normative premise supplied
rules.why: Moore + Hume. Cannot derive ought from is alone. Foundation of metaethics. Standard critique of evolutionary ethics, etc.

rules.name: incompleteness_limits_formal_systems
if: formal system rich enough for arithmetic
rules.why: Gödel 1931. Foundation of foundations. Implications for AI (Lucas, Penrose claims), philosophy of math. Not refutation of AI but cautionary.

rules.name: induction_unjustified_classically
if: inductive inference attempted from past to future
rules.why: Hume's problem. All science depends on. Resolutions: pragmatism, reliability, Bayes (begs question). Foundation problem.

rules.name: free_will_compatibilism_dominant_academic
rules.why: Most analytic philosophers compatibilist. Hume, Dennett, Frankfurt. Reconciles agency + determinism. Popular contrary view: libertarian incompatibilism (Kane).

rules.name: ship_of_Theseus_no_unique_answer
if: identity puzzle like Theseus's ship posed
then: choice of identity criterion determines answer
rules.why: No fact of the matter independent of identity convention. Reveals: identity is partly stipulative. Generalises to personal identity.

rules.name: Wittgenstein_meaning_is_use
then: examine how it's used in language games
rules.why: Late Wittgenstein. Anti-representationalism. Influence on ordinary language + pragmatism. Substrate's microtheories embody this.

rules.name: Grice_implicature_pragmatic_inference
if: speaker says X but means more
rules.why: Maxims of conversation. Foundation pragmatics. AI dialogue systems must handle. 'Some' implies 'not all'.

rules.name: extended_mind_externalises_cognition
if: tool plays role mental state would
then: it can be part of cognitive system (Clark + Chalmers)
rules.why: Notebook for memory; substrate for reasoning. Counters skull-bound mind. Foundation of 4E cognition. Aligned with substrate's design.

rules.name: Turing_test_behavioural_pragmatic
rules.why: Turing avoided 'do machines think?'. Sidesteps consciousness. LLMs pass conversationally; hard-problem questions remain. Foundation.

rules.name: value_alignment_active_problem
rules.why: Foundation of alignment. Reward hacking, instrumental convergence. Substrate's authored-not-trained sidesteps optimisation pathologies.

rules.name: entity_not_program_substrate_position
rules.why: Substrate's design philosophy. Behaviour from drives + environment, not specification. Affects ethics: how to think about an entity, not a tool.
